questions.knowledge_point: Finding the X-Intercepts of a Hyperbola
questions.problem: Calculate the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola $7{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}=7.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} & =7 \\ 7{x}^{2}-{0}^{2} & =7 \\ 7{x}^{2} & =7 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts are $(\pm 1,0).$

questions.problem: Calculate the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{7}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{7} & =1 \\ \frac{(0+2)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{7} & =1 \\ \frac{4}{5}-\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{7} & =1 \\ -\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{7} & =1-\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{7} & =\frac{1}{5} \\ (x-3)^{2} & =-\frac{7}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

We cannot take the square root of a negative number. Therefore, the equation has no real solutions.
So, there are no $x$-intercepts.

questions.problem: Calculate the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(0-2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ 1-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9} & =0 \\ (x+2)^{2} & =0 \\ x+2 & =0 \\ x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $(-2,0).$

questions.problem: Calculate the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{16}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(0-2)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{4}{5}-\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ -\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{16} & =1-\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{16} & =\frac{1}{5} \\ (y+4)^{2} & =-\frac{16}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

We cannot take the square root of a negative number. Therefore, the equation has no real solutions. So, there are no $y$-intercepts.

questions.problem: Calculate the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}=1.$

To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(0)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ (y-1)^{2} & =4 \\ y-1 & =\pm 2 \\ y & =-1,3\end{aligned}

Therefore, the $y$-intercepts are $(0,-1)$ and $(0,3).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5}-(x-2)^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5}-(0-2)^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5}-4 & =1 \\ \frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5} & =5 \\ (y+5)^{2} & =25 \\ y+5 & =\pm 5 \\ y & =-10,0\end{aligned}

$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the horizontal line $y=1$ at the points $(\pm 3,1).$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{10}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{10}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{10} & =1 \\ (x+1)^{2} & =10 \\ x+1 & =\pm \sqrt{10} \\ x & =-1\pm \sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts are $\left(-1\pm \sqrt{10},0\right).$

$\dfrac{x^2}{10}-\dfrac{y^2}{15}=1$
intersects the line $y=-3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=-3,$ we substitute $y=-3$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{15} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{(-3)^{2}}{15} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{9}{15} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{3}{5} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}-6 & =10 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the horizontal line $y=-3$ at the points $(\pm 4, -3).$
